title: Permissions Reference
summary: Single reference for permission keys, effective access behavior, and role fallback logic.
coverage: How permission checks impact UI and APIs

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Permission checks are enforced on both frontend visibility and backend routes. UI access alone never guarantees API authorization.

sections.title: Authorization model
paragraphs: RAPTOR computes effective permissions from three inputs: role defaults, optional permissions stored for the user, and admin full-access behavior. The backend is authoritative and performs permission validation for every protected endpoint.
For non-admin users, optional permissions are sanitized against a role-specific allowlist before storage and when evaluated. Invalid or unknown permission values are ignored.

sections.title: Optional permission extensions
paragraphs: Only `user` and `pentester` roles support optional permission extensions. Manager and admin roles do not accept optional extensions.
Changing role through user administration resets stored optional permissions to an empty set. Optional grants must be explicitly reapplied after role transition when needed.

sections.title: Route and endpoint enforcement patterns
paragraphs: Most APIs are protected by `@permission_required(...)`. Sensitive admin flows additionally require `@admin_required`, which enforces role, session validity, and reset-required blocking.

sections.title: Record-level pentest access constraints
paragraphs: Permission alone is not sufficient for pentest record operations. RAPTOR also enforces record-level access with assignment checks.
Users without `modify_others_pentests_admin` can operate only on records assigned to their username, and unassigned pentest rows are blocked until assignment is set.
